growth has two components: parenchyma (neoplastic cells) and supporting stroma (nonneoplastic; eg, blood vessels, connective tissue).

sourceEvidence.claim: The five station definitions with their row labels — Normal cells (basal → apical polarity, cervical example); Dysplasia (pleomorphism, lost orientation, ↑ nuclear:cytoplasmic ratio, often reversible); Carcinoma in situ/preinvasive (irreversible, entire thickness, intact basement membrane); Invasive carcinoma (collagenases and hydrolases [metalloproteinases]; E-cadherin inactivation); Metastasis (distant organ(s) via lymphatics or blood)
sourceEvidence.quote:
Normal cells

Normal cells with basal → apical polarity. See cervical example, which shows normal cells and
spectrum of dysplasia, as discussed below.

Dysplasia

Loss of uniformity in cell size and shape (pleomorphism); loss of tissue orientation; nuclear
changes (eg, ↑ nuclear:cytoplasmic ratio); often reversible.

Carcinoma in situ/
preinvasive

Irreversible severe dysplasia that involves the entire thickness of epithelium but does not
penetrate the intact basement membrane.

Invasive carcinoma

Cells have invaded basement membrane using collagenases and hydrolases (metalloproteinases).
Cell-cell contacts lost by inactivation of E-cadherin.

Metastasis

Spread to distant organ(s) via lymphatics or blood.

sourceEvidence.claim: The nomenclature rules — carcinoma implies epithelial origin, sarcoma denotes mesenchymal origin, both imply malignancy; benign tumors well-differentiated, well-demarcated, low mitotic activity, no metastases, no necrosis; malignant tumors poor differentiation, erratic growth, local invasion, metastasis, ↓ apoptosis
sourceEvidence.quote:
Carcinoma implies epithelial origin, whereas sarcoma denotes mesenchymal origin. Both terms
generally imply malignancy.
Benign tumors are usually well-differentiated and well-demarcated, with low mitotic activity, no
metastases, and no necrosis.
Malignant tumors (cancers) may show poor differentiation, erratic growth, local invasion,
metastasis, and ↓ apoptosis.
sourceEvidence.verifiedHow: pdftotext text-layer containment on pinned pages (verify-evidence.ts)

sourceEvidence.claim: The malformation pair — hamartoma (disorganized overgrowth of native tissues, Peutz-Jeghers polyps) vs choristoma (normal tissue in a foreign location, gastric tissue in distal ileum in Meckel diverticulum)
sourceEvidence.quote:
Terms for non-neoplastic malformations include hamartoma (disorganized overgrowth of tissues in
their native location, eg, Peutz-Jeghers polyps) and choristoma (normal tissue in a foreign location,
eg, gastric tissue located in distal ileum in Meckel diverticulum).

Degree of invasion and spread from initial
site. Depth of invasion correlates to risk of
metastasis. Based on clinical (c) or pathologic
(p) findings.
TNM staging system (importance: M > N > T):

▘ Regional lymph node metastasis.

grade (eg, a high-stage yet low-grade tumor is
